deskyard forward: map TCP ports between this machine and the computer

Usage: deskyard [-c COMPUTER] forward [-R] PORT[:PORT]...

Maps TCP ports both ways until Ctrl-C, over the remote access API (no port is
opened anywhere else). Each argument is one mapping. PORT or LOCAL:COMPUTER:
this machine's 127.0.0.1:LOCAL becomes localhost:COMPUTER in the computer (a
dev server here, reachable by the computer's browser). -R PORT or -R
COMPUTER:LOCAL (reverse; one -R before each such mapping): the computer's
localhost:COMPUTER becomes 127.0.0.1:LOCAL here. Both ends listen on loopback
only; the computer won't listen below 1024 (plain forward only; -R just dials,
so -R 80:8080 works). A port in use on either side fails that mapping, which
is retried, and the others carry on. When the connection drops (the computer
stops or restarts, the network blips) it keeps its local listeners, closes
open connections and reconnects with backoff (1 s up to 30 s). It exits only
on Ctrl-C, or when the credential is refused. Run it in the background. Inside
a computer it needs -c too.

Arguments:
  PORT       string...   required  a mapping: PORT or LOCAL:COMPUTER; after -R, PORT or COMPUTER:LOCAL

Options:
  -R, --reverse        the next mapping is reverse: a port in the computer
                       becomes a port here

Prints: one line per mapping each time it goes live: "in LOCAL COMPUTER" or
  "out COMPUTER 127.0.0.1:LOCAL"; on stderr one line per state change
  (linked, lost and retrying, port in use)

Examples:
  deskyard -c alice forward 3000 -R 5173
  deskyard -c alice forward 8080:3000 &
  deskyard -c alice forward -R 9229:19229

Where: on the chosen computer (-c COMPUTER); inside a computer too, since it maps ports between two machines. Ports are LOCAL:COMPUTER, or COMPUTER:LOCAL after -R. The computer won't listen below 1024. "Linked to ..." and the out lines appear when the link is accepted, before the computer side is known to run
Exit codes: 0 after Ctrl-C, 1 when the credential is refused (401) or no computer is chosen, 2 usage error
